whatThePageStates: The page is a catalogue of the GuardDuty finding types that are generated from Amazon EKS audit logs. It opens with a Topics list of 33 finding-type links, then repeats each finding type as an H2 section containing an H3 title sentence, a bold 'Default severity' line, a single bullet '**Feature:** EKS audit logs', a description, and remediation advice. There are no tables and no matrix: the only enumeration on the page is the list of finding types themselves. Every entry states resource_type EKSCluster and every entry is attributed to the same detection source, EKS audit logs. The page makes no statement about Regions, about other AWS services, or about anything GuardDuty does NOT detect.

features.featureName: EKS Protection (EKS audit log monitoring) finding types
features.statuses: 33 supported / present, 0 not-supported. Split by section type: 25 non-anomaly-detection finding types (CredentialAccess x4, DefenseEvasion x4, Discovery x4, Execution:Kubernetes/ExecInKubeSystemPod x1, Impact x4, Persistence x4, Policy x4) + 8 AnomalousBehavior finding types = 33. Cross-checked three independent ways: 33 bullets in the Topics list, 33 H2 finding sections (the 34th H2 is 'See also', which is boilerplate, not a finding), and 33 occurrences of the '**Feature: **EKS audit logs' bullet. Severity split also sums to 33: 17 High + 12 Medium + 1 'Medium\*' (RoleBindingCreated, escalates to High for admin/cluster-admin bindings) + 2 Low + 1 'Low\*' (Execution:Kubernetes/AnomalousBehavior.WorkloadDeployed, escalates to Medium for suspicious image or launch command) = 33. Presence in the catalogue is the only status the page carries; there is no Yes/No/Partial column anywhere, and no finding type is listed as unavailable or excluded, so nothing here is a stated 'No'.
features.scope: None on the coverage axis. The page's only qualifier is the constant '**Feature:** EKS audit logs' on every entry, which names the single detection source rather than partitioning the list, and resource_type EKSCluster, likewise constant. Default severity is a per-finding attribute (with two asterisked conditional escalations), not a coverage scope. No Region, plan, tier, or scan-method dimension appears.
features.reasoning: The page enumerates named GuardDuty finding types (CredentialAccess:Kubernetes/MaliciousIPCaller and so on) that GuardDuty publishes about its own detection catalogue, so the axis is findingType and the kind is catalogue. The unit of claim is one finding type = one detection GuardDuty can raise from EKS audit logs; the H2 sections and the Topics bullets are exactly one-to-one with that unit, so the rows do not collapse and distinctTargets is not needed.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' heading and its own bullet list are a table of contents duplicating the H2 sections - counting both would double to 66. The two '**Note**' blocks (the suppression-rules advice near the top, and the Kubernetes 1.14 system:unauthenticated ClusterRoles warning) are guidance, not coverage. The per-finding '**Default severity:**' lines and the two asterisked severity-escalation Notes are severity metadata, not a Yes/No status. The '**Feature: **EKS audit logs' bullets are a constant label, not 33 separate features. The repeated 'Remediation recommendations:' headings and their prose, and the recurring links to Remediating EKS Protection findings, Suppression rules in GuardDuty, Remediating potentially compromised AWS credentials, and the EKS Security best practices guide, are navigation. The trailing 'See also' section is the AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate and must be ignored entirely; the H2 count is 34 only because of it. Anchor tags (<a name=...>) and the '_description' anchors are markup.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The word 'region' does not appear on the page; it gives zero Region coverage and any per-Region figure drawn from it is fabricated. SERVICE: effectively a single service context - Amazon GuardDuty is the detecting service and Amazon EKS is the monitored one; the page does not enumerate services and yields no service-count. RESOURCE TYPE: one, and only as a constant - the intro states all these findings have a resource_type of EKSCluster. That is a single stated value, not an enumeration, so this page supports no resource-type breadth figure either. The only countable dimension the page supplies is 33 finding types.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting the page twice: the 33-item Topics list and the 33 H2 sections describe the same finding types, so a naive 'count every bullet and every heading' parser reports 66. Runners-up: (1) including the trailing 'See also' H2 and reporting 34 finding types; (2) treating the 33 '**Feature: **EKS audit logs' bullets as a second axis or as 33 distinct features when it is one constant label; (3) reading the asterisked severities ('Medium\*', 'Low\*') as a Partial / tri-state status when they are conditional severity escalations, not coverage states; (4) inferring a not-supported claim - the page never says any finding type is unavailable, so any 'No' count from this page is invented; (5) mis-splitting on the escaped '\!' in the two WorkloadDeployed\!PrivilegedContainer / WorkloadDeployed\!ContainerWithSensitiveMount names and turning 2 finding types into 4.
